proof.text: Construct the extension adjunction for arbitrary object universe directly: evaluate a map from the extension presheaf on each summand, and inversely sum the components of a map to the restricted module. Direct-sum generator formulas prove the inverse laws and naturality. Compose with the module sheafification adjunction. This is the construction in LocalizedModuleAdjunctionExact generalized privately without its small-site and precoverage restrictions.

For F on the slice and G,H on the base, extend each component of a map F tensor G|U to H|U bilinearly over the direct-sum extension of F. Its inverse evaluates on the summand at V to U, tensored with the identity of G(V). On generators of the direct sum and tensor product these constructions are inverse, commute with restriction, commute with postcomposition by H to H-prime, and commute with simultaneous parameter maps in F and G. A private natural isomorphism with identity maps on section tensors identifies the simple presheaf restriction model with the underlying presheaf of the sheaf restriction functor.

The unit from the extension presheaf of F to its sheafification is locally injective and locally surjective. Apply tensor-local-bijection descent to its tensor with G. The natural sheafified tensor map is therefore an isomorphism, comparing the sheafification of the raw extension tensor with the right-hand tensor functor. Compare the independent-universe tensor construction with Mathlib presheaf tensor by identity maps on section tensor products.

Compose the Hom equivalences of the extension adjunction, slice sheafification adjunction, identity-on-sections restriction comparison, direct-sum tensor equivalence, inverse base sheafification adjunction, and the preceding natural isomorphism. The private HomData structure records both naturality laws; its composition and inverse operations prove that they hold for the composite.

theorem ringedSlice_extension_tensor_hom_data
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    [(J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [HasWeakSheafify (J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}] :
    let S := SheafOfModules.{max u v} ((sheafCompose J
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R)
    let T := SheafOfModules.{max u v} (((sheafCompose J
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R).over U)
    ∃ e : ∀ X : T × S, ∀ H : S,
      (((ringedSliceTensorLeft.{uC, u, v} J R U).obj X ⟶ H) ≃
        ((ringedSliceTensorRight.{uC, u, v} J R U).obj X ⟶ H)),
      (∀ (X : T × S) (H K : S)
          (φ : (ringedSliceTensorLeft.{uC, u, v} J R U).obj X ⟶ H) (h : H ⟶ K),
        e X K (φ ≫ h) = e X H φ ≫ h) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : T × S) (H : S) (f : X ⟶ Y)
          (φ : (ringedSliceTensorLeft.{uC, u, v} J R U).obj Y ⟶ H),
        e X H ((ringedSliceTensorLeft.{uC, u, v} J R U).map f ≫ φ) =
          (ringedSliceTensorRight.{uC, u, v} J R U).map f ≫ e Y H φ)
